claims.statement: Observability exposes exactly two public doors: `Observability` (one per `UseFramework`, holding the bus's identity, status and span/error API) and the module-level `process` singleton (`ProcessObservability`) for the transport around the buses; the rest of the framework never imports opentelemetry, sentry_sdk, or anything under `observability.errors` / `observability.tracing`, and those subpackages are deliberately not re-exported.

Nothing on the tracing path raises and nothing is required: a missing SDK, an unset endpoint, a broken provider or an exporter that explodes all degrade to a `ComponentStatus` (active/state/reason, with `failure_of` taking the exception text or class name truncated to 200 characters) that the caller reads instead of an exception the bus must survive; with neither extra installed every method is a no-op and the bus runs unchanged.

`_shielded` in span_execution is the guard that keeps observability from changing bus semantics: it catches failures while entering and exiting a context manager, but re-raises the wrapped block's own exception and deliberately ignores a suppressing `__exit__`, so a broken exporter or span processor can neither break an execution nor swallow a business error.

`ObservabilityIdentity.service_name` is `artifact:version:bus` with empty segments omitted and values taken verbatim (no `-`→`_` normalization, which used to mangle both the distribution name and versions like `18.5.0-rc2`), while `release` — the GlitchTip half — drops the bus so two buses of one deployment share one release, falling back to the bus as the artifact only when no artifact resolved.

`resolve_identity` evaluates sources lazily in order — explicit `package=`/`version=`, the library that built the bus via the module→distribution `_`→`-` convention, `APP_RELEASE` (named by `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` only when absent), then the ~200 ms `packages_distributions()` scan cached per process — and each source contributes its artifact together with its own version, never one paired with another source's; the caller's module is captured at `UseFramework` construction while the library is still on the stack, and the identity is resolved once, lazily, on first use.

Each bus gets its own `TracerProvider` built with `Resource.create({SERVICE_NAME: identity.service_name})` (so OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and telemetry.sdk.* survive), a `ParentBased(root=...)` sampler derived from `otlp_traces_sample_rate` (>=1.0 ALWAYS_ON, <=0.0 ALWAYS_OFF, otherwise TraceIdRatioBased; an upstream decision always wins), and a `BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=endpoint))` where the endpoint is passed explicitly because otherwise the SDK ignores the conf and falls back to its own env var or localhost:4317; the gRPC exporter is preferred and the HTTP one covers for a missing gRPC extra.

Tracer providers are owned by a process-wide `registry` keyed by the bus that owns them (with `registry.reset()` clearing providers, error clients and the announced process identity), which is what makes a second `build_root_bus()` reuse the provider the first one created instead of stacking another exporter on the same bus.

`tracer_for(bus)` resolves the bus's own provider first, then falls back to the host's global provider so a bus can ride the host's OTel setup, and returns `None` when the global provider is one this framework built for a *different* bus — a span exported under another service's name is treated as worse than no span; it also returns `None` rather than raising on a broken provider.

`install_process_provider` installs the framework's own provider in the global slot under the reserved `PROCESS` registry key with the bus segment stripped from its identity, and registers that identity on the registry so transport and buses agree on the version; but it returns `None` without touching anything when the current global provider is anything other than OTel's `ProxyTracerProvider`/`NoOpTracerProvider`, i.e. when a host such as Odoo already owns the global — and `setup()` calls it on every bus build, so one deployment opens exactly one process provider.

The process door offers the transport exactly what the buses do not: `process.identity` (artifact:version with no bus segment, preferring the identity a bus already announced so transport and buses never disagree), `process.status` (who owns the global provider), `process.tracer(name)` (the global tracer used by ASGI/httpx instrumentation, or `None` instead of raising when opentelemetry is absent), `process.bind_logger`/`trace_ids` (active-span ids fed from `current_otel_context()`), and `process.record_error(error, layer)` which reports under the process release with `kind="instance"` and no bus tag.

`span_execution` opens at most one span per DTO execution, named after the DTO class, carrying `sincpro.layer` and (only when the bus name is non-empty) `sincpro.instance`, and binds that span's ids to the shared logger; it is called with `layer="feature"` from `FeatureBus.execute` and `layer="application_service"` from `ApplicationServiceBus.execute`, while `FrameworkBus.execute` opens no span of its own, so an ApplicationService delegating to a Feature yields a parent/child pair in the trace.

`span_error` is the tracing half of failure reporting and does only `span.record_exception(error)` plus `set_status(StatusCode.ERROR, str(error))`, guarded by OTEL_AVAILABLE and a non-None span, never raising and never touching GlitchTip; `Observability.record_error` calls it before forwarding the same exception to the errors backend, so one bus failure lands on the span and in GlitchTip.

`FrameworkSpanContext.__enter__` binds the resolved ids to the shared LoggerProxy (so all three buses report them with no propagation step) and then enters a `FrameworkContext` carrying exactly `trace_id`/`span_id` for `self.context.get(...)`; if the logger refuses it cleans up the already-attached OTel context before re-raising so it cannot leak into the next request, and `__exit__` ends the root span (marking StatusCode.ERROR when an exception is in flight), detaches the token even if ending the span failed, exits both contexts and always returns `False`.

`FrameWorkSpanContext` resolves ids through a fixed order of four paths — adopted active span (`adopt_active=True`, read-only, no new span or context), W3C carrier extraction via `TraceContextTextMapPropagator`, explicit hex ids built into a remote `NonRecordingSpan` with SAMPLED flags (a `ValueError` skips only the OTel attachment and still returns the strings for log correlation), and a fresh root span named after the bus taken from the bus's own provider — and every path that cannot obtain a valid OTel span context falls back to fresh UUIDs; without opentelemetry a `carrier` is ignored with a RuntimeWarning naming the missing extra.

`with_trace()` and `with_parent_trace()` differ in trace shape: `with_trace()` adds a root span named after the bounded context (created with `tracer_for(identity.bus)`, so root and DTO spans share one service.name even under a host that registered OTel first), whereas `with_parent_trace()` adopts the host's active span without creating a span or attaching a context, making the bus's DTO spans direct children of the host span with no intermediate level.

`framework.observability.status.otel` reports `off:not_built` before `start()` runs, `off:sdk_missing` when the OTel SDK cannot be imported, `off:no_endpoint` when no endpoint is configured and no real global provider exists, `on:host` when no endpoint is set but the host owns a real provider (the logger still being bound), `on:init` when the bus provider and process provider are up, and `failed:exporter_missing` or `failed:<exception text>` for real misconfiguration — `failed` being the only state that means a misconfiguration rather than a legitimate deployment.

`process.status` answers a different question from the bus status — who owns the global provider transport instrumentation will use — returning `off:sdk_missing` when OTEL_AVAILABLE is false, `on:installed` when the framework registered a provider under the PROCESS registry key, `on:host` when something got there first (Odoo or operator auto-instrumentation), and `off:no_endpoint` when nothing is registered; the PROCESS registry entry is consulted before the global provider, which is what keeps `on:installed` stable for the process lifetime.

`Observability.start(logger)` returns the full `ObservabilityStatus` and emits one line to the instance logger — `observability sentry=<state>:<reason> otel=<state>:<reason>` — at warning level when either backend is `failed` and info otherwise, swallowing a logger that raises; it is invoked from `build_root_bus()`, so the line appears at boot in a service.

In a service that serves HTTP the boot order matters: building each bus installs the process provider that the ASGI middleware needs before it opens its first span, and `process.bind_logger(access_log)` makes the transport's own logger stamp the active request's `trace_id` (never raising when unsupported), so an access-log line, a uvicorn line and the bus's log lines land on the same trace.

Opentelemetry is optional packaging, not a requirement: the `opentelemetry` extra bundles opentelemetry-api, -sdk and both OTLP exporters in `pyproject.toml`, and without it `OTEL_AVAILABLE` is False so `_span_for` returns a `nullcontext` and a Feature's result and exception behaviour are unchanged.
